blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine weather bureau and a South Korean aid agency are advancing a five-year, $12.7-million project to improve flood forecasting and early warnings in Metro Manila and surrounding areas of the Laguna Lake complex. The Project for the Development of Flood Forecasting and Early Warning System (FFEWS) for the Greater Metro Manila and Surrounding Province of Laguna Lake Complex for Disaster Mitigation is being implemented by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) and the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), with support from the Philippine and South Korean governments.
